claims.text: The gps_trace measures 13.92 km between the recorded pickup event (11:26:40) and the recorded dropoff event (11:52:49) against a booking-time optimal of 10.4 km — an excess of 3.52 km, or 33.85% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests therefore pass (excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute), and the route deviation is ESTABLISHED. The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km (13.92); trip_record.actual_distance_km (13.9) is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not cited for the threshold test.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the face of the record: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-04011, all three align on the 11:26:40 trip start and 11:52:49 trip end to the second, and the excess measured from an unimpaired trace (3.52 km / 33.85%) clears the POL-RD-01 threshold. The burden accordingly shifts to the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke an exculpatory provision.

The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 and no down-weighting arises: 158 fixes at a 10 second cadence, the largest interval between consecutive fixes is 10 seconds (well under the 90 second limb (a) gap), the largest straight-line step between consecutive fixes is 108.4 m (well under the 500 m limb (b) jump), and the sustained sampling interval of 10 seconds is nowhere near the 30 second limb (c) figure. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration.

The driver's explanation — 'I followed the navigation app' — is an external-cause assertion tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and it fails that test. The bundle's only advisory artifact, EV-ADVIS-04011-01, is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and under POL-RD-08 the assertion carries no weight and neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal. I disclose that this artifact is impaired: it is cited precisely because its absence is itself citable.

The absent advisory does not convert this case into an escalation. The driver names no evidence id for any advisory, so the missing advisory is not 'an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact' within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. Under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route, on the money track.

No part of the excess is attributable to a rider instruction, so nothing is excluded from the excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The chat log holds two messages only; neither was sent by way of a detour request, neither carries a waypoint_hint, and neither names a road, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run at all on this record and the clause is unavailable — the case is decided on the remaining clauses.

The driver cannot shrink the excess by way of a relocated endpoint. trip_record.pickup_amended_at and trip_record.dropoff_amended_at are both null, no original_pickup or original_dropoff is stored, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are both null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against and the booked optimal of 10.4 km / 19 min stands as the baseline.

The remedy is arithmetic under POL-RD-02 and the trip is METERED (quoted_fare_sgd null, fare_model METERED), so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 10.4 optimal km + 0.28 x 19 optimal min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharge + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 17.72. Refund = charged_total 22.32 - recomputed_fare 17.72 = SGD 4.60, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and is 20.6% of charged_total (not 90% or more), so the correct outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.60 to the rider.

The surge multiplier used in that computation was read from the fare_breakdown, the only artifact that carries the field: EV-FARE-04011 records surge_multiplier 1.0 and surge_amount 0.00, so no uplift is applied to the recomputed fare and the recomputation is not distorted in either direction.

No pass-through line inflates or double-counts this award. The fare_breakdown itemises zero ERP gantries and zero tolls and carries no airport surcharge, so there is no POL-RD-09 correction to add on top of the 4.60; the distance-and-time refund computed under POL-RD-02 is the whole of the rider's monetary remedy on this trip.

The rider's own dispute history does not raise the bar on this claim. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the figure of 4 that POL-RD-08 uses to require corroboration beyond the gps_trace for a sub-30% excess, and this claim is in any event measured from an unimpaired trace; the rider's account age, rating and lifetime trip count are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not cited as grounds.

The rider's '$6 back' is a round-figure estimate of what the detour cost him, not a measured figure; the policy fixes the remedy arithmetically and the measured entitlement on this record is SGD 4.60. Awarding that amount leaves the rider paying for the route he booked (10.4 km, 19 min, SGD 17.72) rather than for the 13.92 km the vehicle actually drove, which is the whole of what this claim asks the tribunal to correct.

claims.text: On the platform's own trace the detour is exactly 3.52 km over a booked optimal of 10.4 km, or 33.85% - it clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and stops there; nothing in the record corroborates the rider's picture of a much longer Yio Chu Kang Road / Upper Thomson detour beyond that measured figure, and the trace that fixes it is complete (158 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gap above 10 s, largest step 108.4 m), so the excess is bounded at 3.52 km and no more.

The deviation is measured but not MATERIAL: 33.85% is below the 50% percentage gate and 3.52 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate under POL-RD-01, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered by materiality and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b), which requires a deviation that is both material and substantiated on this trip, is unavailable. The remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial and nothing more.

Even if POL-RD-06 is consulted, the driver shows no repeat-deviation pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 260, a ratio of 0.00 well below the 0.05 threshold and below the alternative three-flag test, so no balance is resolved against him, no uplift attaches and no driver-conduct referral follows. No other field on either profile is relied on, per POL-GEN-01.

The refund is arithmetic and cannot exceed 4.60: charged_total of 22.32 less the recomputed optimal-route fare of 17.72 - (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.4 + 0.28 x 19) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo - leaves 4.60, and 4.60 is only 20.6% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would convert a partial into a full refund.

The rider's premise that this trip is 'usually about 16 bucks' is contradicted by the platform's own figures: the booked optimal distance and duration price the same journey at 17.72, so the 6.00 contested is anchored on a fare the evidence does not support and the maximum the policy can move is 4.60.

Nothing on this trip engages the pass-through limb: no ERP gantry was charged, erp_lines is empty on both the optimal and off-optimal sides, tolls_erp is 0.00, and the 0.00 airport surcharge sits on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport - so no POL-RD-09 correction may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in it and could never be counted twice.

It is bounded at that figure: nothing in the record supports a longer Yio Chu Kang Road / Upper Thomson detour than the 3.52 km the trace shows, and the trace is complete (158 fixes, 10-second cadence, largest step 108.4 m).

Consulted anyway, the driver shows no repeat-deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d = 0 against 260 completed trips in 90 days), so there is no balance to tip, no FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b), and no driver-conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c).

THE MONEY. The trip is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and no route under POL-RD-11 is open. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 10.4 optimal km + 0.28 x 19 optimal min) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-04011) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharge + 0 waiting fee - 0 promo = 17.72. Refund = charged_total 22.32 - 17.72 = 4.60. That is above the 0.50 de-minimis floor and is 20.6% of the charge (not the 90% or more that would convert this to a full refund), so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 4.60. The rider's figures are not adopted: 'usually about 16 bucks' is contradicted by the platform's own booking-time pricing of 17.72, and the '$6 back' is a round-figure estimate rather than a measured entitlement.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. 'I followed the navigation app' is an assertion of an external traffic cause, and it is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory (EV-ADVIS-04011-01) is MISSING, weight 0.0, no payload, so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. It neither reduces the measured excess nor supplies an amended optimal. It also does not escalate the case: the driver names no advisory identifier, so under POL-RD-13(1) the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle, not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5). Because the trace itself is clean (no gap over 90 s, no step over 500 m, no sampling interval over 30 s), it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c), no independent corroboration is needed and POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged.

OTHER CLAUSES. No rider instruction in the chat log asks for a detour or names a road or waypoint, so POL-RD-04 excludes nothing from the excess and no DRIVER_COMPENSATION arises (the billed 13.92 km equals the trace, so there is no unbilled shortfall). No pickup or dropoff was amended, so POL-RD-05 does not apply and the booked 10.4 km baseline stands. No ERP gantry, toll or airport surcharge was charged, so no POL-RD-09 correction is added on top of the 4.60 and none could be counted twice. All charge lines reconcile, so POL-RD-10(8) is not triggered.

CONFIDENCE AND EFFECT. Confidence is 0.90: the deciding facts (trace distance, optimal distance, the fare arithmetic) are carried by artifacts at full weight 1.0. The monetary effect of 4.60 is below the 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so it executes on issue. Both parties may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: this is a route deviation, and the refund is fixed by the policy arithmetic rather than by what either side asks for. Both advocates read the record the same way and I agree with them.

WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS. The trip record (EV-TRIP-04011), the GPS trace (EV-GPS-04011) and the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-04011) all carry trip id TRP-04011 and align to the second on the 11:26:40 start and the 11:52:49 finish. The GPS trace measures the distance actually driven at 13.92 km; under POL-RD-01 that trace figure governs, and the trip record's 13.9 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and is not used for the threshold test. The booked optimal route was 10.4 km and 19 minutes. The excess is therefore 3.52 km, or 33.85% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass — the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms — so the deviation is established.

TRACE INTEGRITY. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes: 158 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no interval above 10 seconds, largest straight-line step 108.4 m. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) do not fire, so no down-weighting and no corroboration requirement arises.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The driver's account ('I followed the navigation app; did not go the long way on purpose') cites no evidence id and no clause, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight and does not reduce the measured excess or supply an amended optimal route. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-04011-01, is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload — so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and the excuse is weightless under POL-RD-13. Because the driver named no evidence id for that advisory, its absence is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5), and the case is decided on the money track rather than escalated.

NO RIDER-SIDE EXONERATION. POL-RD-04 does not apply: the chat log (EV-CHAT-04011) holds two messages, neither a detour request, neither carrying a waypoint_hint, and neither naming a road, so nothing is excluded from the excess. POL-RD-05 does not apply: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and the amended optimal fields are null, so the booked 10.4 km / 19 min stands as the baseline.

THE REMEDY. The trip is METERED (quoted_fare_sgd null), so POL-RD-11 does not close the distance route and POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 10.4 km + 0.28 x 19 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 16.92 + 0.80 = 17.72. The 1.0 surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries the field. Refund = charged_total 22.32 - 17.72 = 4.60, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 4.60. That exceeds the 0.50 de minimis floor and is 20.6% of the charge, well short of the 90% that would convert a partial into a full refund. No ERP, toll, waiting or surcharge line exists, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top and nothing is double-counted.

THE RIDER'S $6. The $6 figure and the 'usually about 16 bucks' premise are not supported by the evidence: the platform's own optimal-route fare for this journey is 17.72, so the measured entitlement is 4.60.

DRIVER COMPENSATION AND REFERRALS. No driver compensation arises: the rider was not billed for less distance than the trace records. No POL-RD-06 conduct pattern exists (deviation_flags_90d 0 against 260 completed trips in 90 days), so there is no conduct referral, and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer. The referrals list is empty.

CONFIDENCE AND EXECUTION. The ruling rests only on weight-1.0 artifacts, so confidence is not capped below 1.0; I set it at 0.90. The monetary effect of SGD 4.60 is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so the refund executes automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04. One rider claim was discarded at the mechanical check for citing the impaired advisory without disclosing its issue code; its substance is preserved by a separate kept claim that does disclose the impairment.

Under POL-RD-13 the deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route, on the money track.

ledger.claim: The rider's '$6 back' is a round-figure estimate of what the detour cost him, not a measured figure; the policy fixes the remedy arithmetically and the measured entitlement on this record is SGD 4.60. Awarding that amount leaves the rider paying for the route he booked (10.4 km, 19 min, SGD 17.72) rather than for the 13.92 km the vehicle actually drove, which is the whole of what this claim asks the tribunal to correct.

On the platform's own trace the detour is exactly 3.52 km over a booked optimal of 10.4 km, or 33.85% - it clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km) and stops there; nothing in the record corroborates the rider's picture of a much longer Yio Chu Kang Road / Upper Thomson detour beyond that measured figure, and the trace that fixes it is complete (158 fixes, 10 s cadence, no gap above 10 s, largest step 108.4 m), so the excess is bounded at 3.52 km and no more.

The deviation is measured but not MATERIAL: 33.85% is below the 50% percentage gate and 3.52 km is below the 8.0 km absolute gate under POL-RD-01, so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered by materiality and the FULL_REFUND uplift in POL-RD-06(b), which requires a deviation that is both material and substantiated on this trip, is unavailable. The remedy is the POL-RD-02 partial and nothing more.

Even if POL-RD-06 is consulted, the driver shows no repeat-deviation pattern: deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 260, a ratio of 0.00 well below the 0.05 threshold and below the alternative three-flag test, so no balance is resolved against him, no uplift attaches and no driver-conduct referral follows. No other field on either profile is relied on, per POL-GEN-01.

The refund is arithmetic and cannot exceed 4.60: charged_total of 22.32 less the recomputed optimal-route fare of 17.72 - (3.80 + 0.75 x 10.4 + 0.28 x 19) x the 1.0 surge multiplier read from the fare_breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, no surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo - leaves 4.60, and 4.60 is only 20.6% of the charge, far below the 90% share that would convert a partial into a full refund.

The rider's premise that this trip is 'usually about 16 bucks' is contradicted by the platform's own figures: the booked optimal distance and duration price the same journey at 17.72, so the 6.00 contested is anchored on a fare the evidence does not support and the maximum the policy can move is 4.60.

Nothing on this trip engages the pass-through limb: no ERP gantry was charged, erp_lines is empty on both the optimal and off-optimal sides, tolls_erp is 0.00, and the 0.00 airport surcharge sits on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport - so no POL-RD-09 correction may be added on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and any off-route ERP would in any event already be comprehended in it and could never be counted twice.
